title: Diagnostic Value of an AI-Based Software Solution for the Automated Classification of Lesions in Prostate MRI
summary:
The study investigates whether an AI program (a type of “artificial intelligence”) can assist in evaluating MRI images of the prostate, and whether it can detect potentially malignant changes in the prostate as well as, or even better than, experienced radiologists.
The study examines how well this program—called mdprostate®, developed by the Berlin-based company mediaire—performs in comparison to experienced doctors, and whether it can help make the assessment of prostate MRIs more reliable, consistent, and possibly even faster.

interventions.name: The study includes patients aged 18 and older who have undergone a prostate MRI (either mpMRI with contrast agent or bpMRI without contrast agent) with a diagnostic image quality of PI-QUAL 4/5 since 2021.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Prostate MRI in-house (with contrast agent/mpMRI and without contrast agent/biparametric)
- MRI (bpMRI), period starting from 2021
- Diagnostic image quality (PI-QUAL 4/5)
Exclusion criteria:
- Low image quality (PI-QUAL 3 or lower)
- Status post focal therapies of the prostate such as high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU), vascular photodynamic therapy (VPT), radiation therapy, transurethral resection of the prostate (TUR-P), holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP), prostate artery embolization (PAE)
